turns.input: *Nicco watches from the shadows as Varro Kest inspects Edda Marn, a grown woman held in chains, and tells her what she is worth to him.*
turns.draft:
The alley stinks of standing water and old smoke. Varro Kest moves down the line of captives with the unhurried air of a man browsing cloth, and stops in front of the woman whose wrists are chained to the ring in the wall. He takes her chin in one ringed hand, turns her face toward the light, and lets go.

"Edda Marn," he says, tasting the name. "Grown, healthy, good teeth. A debt-taker, so the paper's clean." He steps back and looks her over like a man appraising a horse. "Eight, maybe nine silver on a good day. Less if you keep sulling up like that and bruise your own face before I can sell you."

Edda says nothing. She stares past him at the wet stones, her arms hanging as far as the chains allow, breathing slow and even through her nose. Somewhere behind the shuttered walls a dog barks twice and goes quiet.

Varro shrugs at her silence and pulls a folded scrap of paper from his coat, checking something written on it. "Buyer comes through tomorrow, wants kitchen stock. You'll do. One night in the cold, girl, that's all this is." He tucks the paper away and glances up the alley, where a big man in unfamiliar clothes stands watching from the shadow of a doorway — close enough that Varro's eyes narrow slightly. "You lost, friend? This isn't the front market."
